messages:
carmen: Heads-up — seeing repeated 99th pct tail spikes in eu-west1 between 02:10–02:30 UTC. Patterns point at a small set of tenants hitting egress/KV heavy tails while running in fractional dedicated pools. Can we talk egress fencing (soft caps + routing fallback) as a short-term mitigation? :thinking:

ben: do you have the query + example tenant IDs?

carmen: query pasted below, and a sample tenant: tenant-42
```
sum(rate(kv_outbound_bytes{region=\"eu-west1\"}[5m])) by (tenant)
```

alex: infra-bot shows alert: eu-west1_kv_egress_spike firing 5x in last 20m (matches). infra-bot:alert_id=eu-kv-8943

infra-bot: Alert eu-west1_kv_egress_spike started at 2024-06-11T02:12:03Z, severity=warning, hits=5

marie: If we fence egress on fractional dedicated slices we reduce noisy neighbor surface, but we risk throttling latency-sensitive customers. Need a cost SLO tradeoff — how many requests are we dropping vs rerouting?

ben: we can implement soft egress caps per-slice + automatic reroute to shared-hosted if cap exceeded. Suggested flow: 1) soft-cap (90th pct) triggers 2) attempt KV-prefetch/backoff 3) reroute to fallback model variant / region 4) flag tenant for ops review.

alex: routing constraints: fallback to shared-hosted will add cross-region egress for some tenants; we should prefer same-region hosted if available. Also need to update routing table entries: 
```
- route: eu-west1.multipool -> preferred: eu-west1.hosted, fallback: eu-west2.hosted
- policy: soft-fence -> allow 30s burst, then reroute
```

carmen: +1 on same-region preference. For detection, suggest combining kv_outbound rate with per-gpu context-switch and nvlink errors to avoid false positives. Example alert heuristic: 
```
WHEN kv_rate(tenant) > X AND gpu_ctx_switches > Y AND nvlink_errs > 0 FOR 2m
```

marie: What about cost? Rerouting to hosted adds per-token billing; fencing reduces shared pool degradation (so net cost might be neutral). Need an estimate: how many tokens are being moved. Carmen, can you attach a 1h sample?

carmen: sample attached (snippet): tenant-42: 1.2M outbound bytes in 10m window, ~45k tokens equivalent -> ~+$0.12/min if rerouted to hosted at current pricing. But the shared pool tail adds much more infra cost in burst (GPU stall time).

ben: implementation note — prefer eBPF NIC policing at pod level for finer shaping vs coarse tc. We have a prototype eBPF hook in staging: 
```
prog: egress_shaper v0.3
flags: burst=30s, rate=120Mbps, fallback=hosted-eu
```

alex: ops playbook draft: 
- soft-fence auto-reroute enabled for 5% of slices (canary)
- notify owner + create task if tenant rerouted > 3x in 1h
- toggle back if false positive within 10m

marie: agree to canary. Also add a cost center tag when rerouted so billing team can see token shift.

ben: I'll push eBPF pod hooks to staging canary tomorrow. Who owns the automations for tagging + rollback?

carmen: i'll own tagging + alert enrichment. ben, ping me when eBPF PR is up and i'll wire the SLO dashboards.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: egress_shaper v0.3 scheduled to staging at 1719580000 (ETA 10:00 UTC).

alex: thanks — plan looks safe. Only ask: add a metric for "rerouted_tokens" so Optimize can evaluate cost impact.

carmen: will add rerouted_tokens and tenant_reroute_count. Canaries first, full roll after 48h monitoring. :thumbsup:
